scope_decision: Option A - documents/files metadata extended into MongoDB Atlas with Atlas Search indexes; the weekly reindex job is deleted outright rather than rewritten.
legacy_inputs: MeiliSearch documents and files indexes, deleted and recreated on every run
target_objects_note: The shared ow_tp_demo database contains unrelated workshop data, so this unit uses the isolated ow_tp_cronbox_demo namespace and leaves foreign data untouched.

acceptance_checks.description: Document-ID sets are compared, not counts: the Atlas documents collection covers exactly the 125 baseline document ids and the files collection exactly the 72 baseline file ids (the reverse-orphan metadata row is excluded from the file corpus, as it was by the legacy corpus API).

Every golden query is executed against Atlas using the $search aggregation stage (never a regex or $text fallback) and the returned document-ID set equals the baseline MeiliSearch result set for the same query.

Field roles from the legacy MeiliSearch settings are preserved in the Atlas Search index definitions: documents searchable on title/content/tags, filterable on type/owner_id/tags/created_at/updated_at, sortable on updated_at/created_at; files searchable on name/tags/mime_type, filterable on type/owner_id/mime_type/folder_id/tags/created_at/updated_at, sortable on updated_at/created_at/size. Index definitions are read back from the Atlas API.
A multi-byte query term matches its seeded document ('Δocument ☕' in the documents corpus), proving byte-transparent indexing and analysis rather than ASCII folding that loses the term.

Index maintenance is continuous: after inserting one document into the collection it becomes searchable without any reindex job, rebuild step, or index deletion — the weekly delete-and-recreate cycle is gone.
Rerunning the golden query set returns identical document-ID sets (idempotency of the query surface), and no query returns a document outside the corpus.
The legacy job is deleted, not ported: no reindex schedule, no MeiliSearch dependency, and no crontab entry remains after the decommission PR.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Titles, names, content and tags are stored in the collections exactly as served by the source of truth, including multi-byte characters; the search analyzer may normalize for matching but must never alter the stored document values.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: A source field that is not valid UTF-8 is stored as binary and excluded from the analyzed fields rather than lossily coerced.

malformed_record_policy.details: Legacy defaulted every absent field to an empty string and would index a document with an empty id. The migrated corpus must instead attribute records with a missing or empty id: they are excluded from the searchable corpus and reported with their source position, never indexed under a blank key. Documents carrying extra unmodeled fields are stored and indexed on the mapped fields only.

empty_input_semantics.details: Legacy deleted each index and recreated it before ingesting, so an empty corpus left an empty index and destroyed the previous week's searchable state. The Atlas replacement inherits the source-of-truth lifecycle instead: an empty corpus means an empty collection, and no path may delete a populated index in order to rebuild it. This behavioral difference is deliberate and is recorded as the reason the unit is deleted rather than rewritten.

planted_anomalies.description: Document doc-004 carries the title 'Δocument ☕' and must remain findable by that term.
The reverse-orphan file metadata row is absent from the file corpus (72 files, not 73).
The legacy rankingRules ordering (words, typo, proximity, attribute, sort, exactness) has no one-to-one Atlas Search equivalent.
planted_anomalies.reason: Relevance ordering is engine-specific and cannot be reconciled across engines. Acceptance therefore compares returned document-ID sets rather than result ordering or scores, and the golden query set is chosen so every query has an unambiguous expected set.

planted_anomalies.description: MeiliSearch typo tolerance is on by default; Atlas Search fuzziness must be configured explicitly per query.
planted_anomalies.reason: The golden query set uses exact and phrase terms only, so no acceptance check depends on typo-tolerance parity between the two engines.
